For example, if you have a staff of 100 people, but 1000 desktops, laptops, smartphones, and similar devices, you can licence your users with User CALs, Device CALs, or some combination of both. If you only ever have a single instance of each device running, and each user only has access to a single computing device, Device CALs and User CALs would effectively cover the same number of people. If your organisation has many different computers and portable devices, but only a single user in all of those devices, Device CALs will likely be less expensive. However, if each user in your organisation has access to two or more devices, Device CALs would cost you more than User CALs.
You can combine User CALs and Device CALs within your organisation, if different parts of your organisation have different computing patterns. This allows each section of your organisation to be licensed in the most cost-effective manner.

About 10 years later, the Samuelsson, Bergström and Oates teams found there were two enzymes, one called COX-1 and the other COX-2. Both catalyze the formation of prostaglandins, but only COX-2 seems to be required for prostaglandin production following acute tissue injury. They also discovered that aspirin blocks prostaglandin synthesis by interfering with the activity of COX-1 and aspirin-like drugs block COX-2.
The first COX-2 inhibitor, Vioxx, which was manufactured by Merck, hit the market in 1999. By 2004, the annual sales for COX-2 inhibitors were nearing $5 billion.

Port Melbourne's network of immigrants
In 1956, Melbourne hosted the Summer Olympic Games and tens of thousands of visitors arrived in the city via ships docking at Station Pier. Between 1946 and 1970, and directly as a result of those Olympic Games, half a million more people migrated to Australia. Seventy per cent of these people chose Melbourne. Of this, nearly half came from Europe; mainly from Italy, Greece, Germany and Malta. Of the remaining third, the United States, Canada and South Africa were the major contributors.
